title: Where transactions come from and when a commit is uncertain

questions.stem: Inside one Spring bean, methodA() is @Transactional and calls this.methodB(), which is @Transactional(propagation = REQUIRES_NEW). What does methodB run in?

options.text: A new transaction of its own, suspended from methodA's until methodB returns.
options.says: REQUIRES_NEW is applied by the proxy, and a call through this never reaches the proxy, so no new transaction starts.

options.text: No transaction at all, because the annotation is ignored inside a single class.
options.says: methodB is not left without a transaction: it runs inside the one methodA's proxy call already opened.

options.text: methodA's transaction, because the call does not pass through the Spring proxy.
options.says: Self-invocation bypasses the AOP proxy, so methodB's own settings are never applied and it joins methodA's transaction.

questions.stem: The connection drops while commit() is running and the call throws. What does the application know about the transaction?

options.text: Its outcome is unknown, so the application checks it after reconnecting.
options.says: The failure can happen after the database committed but before the answer arrived, so the outcome is unknown until it is checked.

options.text: It was rolled back, since the database discards a commit that throws.
options.says: The exception only says the call failed on the client side; the commit may still have been applied.

options.text: It is still open, so a commit() on a new connection can finish it.
options.says: A transaction belongs to its connection; a new connection cannot commit work begun on the one that dropped.
